Simulate a 2D high-speed compressible supersonic jet using OpenFOAM with the rhoCentralFoam solver.
Treat air as a perfect gas: use hePsiThermo as thermodynamics model, perfectGas as equation of state, and sutherland as transport model in constant/thermophysicalProperties.
Generate a 2D mesh extruded one cell in the z-direction with the frontAndBack patch set to empty.
Set the nozzle inlet patch (supersonic inflow, Mach 2.0) with fixedValue for velocity U = (686 0 0) m/s, temperature T = 300 K, and pressure p = 101325 Pa.
Set far-field and outlet boundaries with waveTransmissive for pressure p and temperature T, and zeroGradient for velocity U.
Set solid walls with noSlip for velocity U.
In system/controlDict set application to rhoCentralFoam, enable adaptive time stepping with a CFL number no greater than 0.5 to satisfy the explicit density-based solver stability constraint.
Place the far-field and outlet boundaries sufficiently far from the nozzle exit to prevent spurious wave reflections from contaminating the supersonic jet region.
Output results at regular intervals sufficient to resolve shock formation and jet mixing structures.
